description: The SOURCE phrase of the RECORD KEY and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clauses (ISO §2023:12.4.5.12.2 / §2023:12.4.5.6.2: record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS { data-name-2 } ...) - a key that is 'the concatenation of all occurrences of data-name-2 in the order specified' (§2023:12.4.5.12.4 GR2 / §2023:12.4.5.6.4 GR2), with the record-key-name word class (§2023:8.3.2.2.24) and its scope (§2023:8.4.6.2.4). A COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): ANSI X3.23-1985 prints `RECORD KEY IS data-name-1` (§1985:IX.2.7.2) and `ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS data-name-1 [ WITH DUPLICATES ]` (§1985:IX.2.5.2) only, data-name-1 one alphanumeric item (§1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2); §2002:12.3.4.12.1 and §2002:12.3.4.5.1 add the `record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS { data-name-2 } ...` arm, §2002:12.3.4.12.3 GR2 / §2002:12.3.4.5.3 GR2 reading 'Record-key-name-1 defines a record key consisting of the concatenation of all occurrences of data-name-2 in the order specified' (§2002:12.3.4.12.2 SR5: 'Record-key-name-1 has the class and category of data-name-2'), and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 110: 'RECORD KEY and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY. Keys for indexed files may be made up from more than one component.' §2014:12.4.4.11.3 GR2 / §2014:12.4.4.5.3 GR2 carry the same sentence, so 2014 = 2023. Annex A.3 item 40 makes the capability processor-dependent; this implementation provides it (kb/Work PB1099 Q1, owner rule R65). Gated in ONE place, VersionConformancePass.VisitRecordKeySourcePhrase - the one grammar rule both clauses share.
display: the SOURCE phrase of the RECORD KEY or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
vcr: RECORD KEY / ALTERNATE RECORD KEY SOURCE phrase (2002; quoted: §2002:F.2 item 110 against §1985:IX.2.7.2); VCR row 7.36
